releaseNotes: Platform release: a founder can take the company's work out of Formation in three shapes — a document to read, a spreadsheet of the numbers, and the structured record for another tool. The thing that makes an export worth building rather than copy-and-paste is lineage: every deliverable leaves with the claims it rests on and the decisions it is linked to, resolved to what they say rather than to their identifiers, because a conclusion handed over with its reasoning removed is not much of a hand-over. A citation that cannot be resolved is counted rather than dropped, so a reader can tell "this cites nothing" from "the citations were lost on the way out".

The bundle is built by naming the fields that may leave, the same discipline as a shared link and a provider request, and what it keeps out matters as much as what it lets through: no conversations, no review requests, no invitations, no sessions, no email addresses, no engine internals. A bundle that quietly carried a private argument between cofounders into a file the founder mailed to an investor would be the same failure as a shared link that did, and a test plants exactly that argument and asserts it does not travel. The manifest states what was deliberately left out, because a reader who cannot see the omissions cannot tell a complete record from a filtered one. The spreadsheet keeps money in minor units and says so in every column header — a column silently mixing pounds and pence is how a spreadsheet ends up off by a hundred. Checks, 237 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
